introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics 3 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2024. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. For your guidance the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated in brackets. Mathematical formulae and tables, published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.

The paper contains eight questions.
incertitudes: Question 8 : les parties a(i)-a(iii) et b(i)-b(ii) sont transcrites chacune comme une question séparée pour porter les points imprimés ; l'énoncé commun de (a) est donc recopié dans chaque partie. Dans b(ii) le sujet écrit P(|x - 1| < 1/2) avec x minuscule : lu comme X.

questions.enonce_markdown: The Admission Committee of a secondary school receives $4$ applications for admission weekly. Given that the probability that any application is granted is $\dfrac{2}{3}$, find the probability that $2$ applications are granted per week. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $X$ be the number of applications granted in a week. The $4$ applications are independent with the same probability of success, so $X\sim B\!\left(4,\tfrac23\right)$ and

$$P(X=k) = \binom{4}{k}\left(\tfrac23\right)^k\left(\tfrac13\right)^{4-k}.$$

$$P(X=2) = \binom42\left(\tfrac23\right)^2\left(\tfrac13\right)^2 = 6\times\frac49\times\frac19 = \frac{24}{81} = \frac{8}{27}\approx 0.296.$$

questions.enonce_markdown: The Admission Committee of a secondary school receives $4$ applications for admission weekly. Given that the probability that any application is granted is $\dfrac{2}{3}$, find the probability that more than $2$ applications are granted each week. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $X$ be the number of applications granted in a week. The $4$ applications are independent with the same probability of success, so $X\sim B\!\left(4,\tfrac23\right)$ and

$$P(X=k) = \binom{4}{k}\left(\tfrac23\right)^k\left(\tfrac13\right)^{4-k}.$$

$$P(X>2) = P(X=3)+P(X=4)$$

$$P(X=3) = \binom43\left(\tfrac23\right)^3\left(\tfrac13\right) = 4\times\frac{8}{27}\times\frac13 = \frac{32}{81},\qquad
P(X=4) = \left(\tfrac23\right)^4 = \frac{16}{81}$$

$$P(X>2) = \frac{32+16}{81} = \frac{48}{81} = \frac{16}{27}\approx 0.593.$$

*Check:* $1-[P(0)+P(1)+P(2)] = 1-\dfrac{1+8+24}{81} = \dfrac{48}{81}$.

questions.enonce_markdown: The Admission Committee of a secondary school receives $4$ applications for admission weekly. Given that the probability that any application is granted is $\dfrac{2}{3}$, find the expected number of applications to be granted each week. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
$X\sim B\!\left(4,\tfrac23\right)$, so the expectation is

$$E(X) = np = 4\times\frac23 = \frac83 \approx 2.67.$$

The expected number of applications granted each week is $\dfrac83$ (about $2.67$).

questions.enonce_markdown: A continuous function $g(x)$ is defined by $g(x) = \begin{cases}\dfrac34(2x-x^2), & 0\le x\le 2\\[2mm] 0, & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$ Show that $g(x)$ is the probability density function of a continuous random variable $X$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
A function is a probability density function if (1) $g(x)\ge0$ for all $x$ and (2) $\displaystyle\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}g(x)\,dx = 1$.

(1) For $0\le x\le2$, $2x-x^2 = x(2-x)\ge0$, so $g(x)\ge0$; elsewhere $g(x)=0$.

(2)
$$\int_0^2\tfrac34(2x-x^2)\,dx = \tfrac34\left[x^2-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^2 = \tfrac34\left(4-\frac83\right) = \tfrac34\times\frac43 = 1.$$

Both conditions hold, so $g$ is a probability density function.

questions.enonce_markdown: A continuous function $g(x)$ is defined by $g(x) = \dfrac34(2x-x^2)$ for $0\le x\le2$ and $0$ otherwise, and is the probability density function of a continuous random variable $X$. Calculate $P\left(\left|x-1\right|<\dfrac12\right)$. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
$|x-1|<\tfrac12 \iff \tfrac12<x<\tfrac32$, and this interval lies inside $[0,2]$. So

$$P\left(|X-1|<\tfrac12\right) = \int_{1/2}^{3/2}\tfrac34(2x-x^2)\,dx = \tfrac34\left[x^2-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{1/2}^{3/2}.$$

At $x=\tfrac32$: $\tfrac94-\tfrac{27/8}{3} = \tfrac94-\tfrac98 = \tfrac98$.

At $x=\tfrac12$: $\tfrac14-\tfrac{1/8}{3} = \tfrac14-\tfrac1{24} = \tfrac{5}{24}$.

$$P = \tfrac34\left(\tfrac98-\tfrac5{24}\right) = \tfrac34\left(\tfrac{27-5}{24}\right) = \tfrac34\times\tfrac{22}{24} = \frac{11}{16} = 0.6875.$$
